analogy: Like C# var/const: let = reassignable local, const = readonly reference. Forget var (like old VB quirks).
analogyDe: Wie C# var/const: let = veränderbar, const = schreibgeschützt (Referenz). var vergessen (wie alte VB-Marotten).
audio: let is for values that change. const is the default. Use const unless you reassign. var is legacy, avoid it.
audioDe: let für Werte, die sich ändern. const ist Standard. const nutzen, außer du weist neu zu. var ist veraltet.
keyPoints: Default to const; use let only when reassigning.
const prevents reassignment, not deep immutability.
var is function-scoped legacy — never use in new code.
keyPointsDe: Standard: const; let nur bei Neuzuweisung.
const verhindert Neuzuweisung, nicht tiefe Unveränderlichkeit.

quiz.explain: Reassignment of a const binding is a compile error.
quiz.explainDe: Neuzuweisung an const ist ein Compile-Fehler.
options: Compile error: cannot assign to PI
quiz.q: const PI = 3.14; PI = 3; — what happens in TS?
quiz.qDe: const PI = 3.14; PI = 3; — was passiert in TS?

title: let, const (and forget var)
tldr: Use const by default, let when you reassign. Never var.
tldrDe: Standard const, let bei Neuzuweisung. Nie var.

analogy: Like C# lambdas (x => x+1) but function is an expression everywhere; callbacks are like C# delegates.
analogyDe: Wie C#-Lambdas, aber Funktionen sind überall Ausdrücke; Callbacks sind wie Delegates.
audio: Arrow functions are short callbacks. One expression means implicit return. this behaves lexically, unlike C# this.
audioDe: Arrow-Funktionen sind kurze Callbacks. Ein Ausdruck heißt implizites return. this ist lexikalisch, anders als in C#.
keyPoints: Arrow with single expression returns implicitly.
Callbacks replace C# delegates/events in JS style.
function vs arrow differ mainly in this binding.
keyPointsDe: Arrow mit einem Ausdruck hat implizites return.
function vs Arrow unterscheiden sich v.a. bei this.

quiz.explainDe: Arrows mit einem Ausdruck geben den Wert zurück.

title: Functions & arrows
tldr: Arrows are lambdas; single expression = implicit return.
tldrDe: Arrows sind Lambdas; ein Ausdruck = implizites return.

analogy: Arrays like List<T>, objects like anonymous types / Dictionary. Destructuring like C# deconstruction.
analogyDe: Arrays wie List<T>, Objekte wie anonyme Typen/Dictionary. Destructuring wie Deconstruction in C#.
audio: Arrays use map filter find. Objects are dictionaries with dot access. Destructure to pull fields out in one line.
audioDe: Arrays mit map, filter, find. Objekte sind Dictionaries mit Punktzugriff. Destructuring holt Felder in einer Zeile.
keyPoints: map/filter/find return new arrays — no mutation.

quiz.explain: map builds a new array; original untouched.
quiz.explainDe: map baut ein neues Array; Original bleibt.

title: Arrays, objects, destructuring
tldr: map/filter/find + object destructuring = 80% of JS reading.

analogy: Like C# async/await with Task<T> — a Promise<T> is a future value.
analogyDe: Wie C# async/await mit Task<T> — Promise<T> ist ein zukünftiger Wert.
audio: Promises are futures. await unwraps them. Always handle rejection with try catch.
audioDe: Promises sind Futures. await entpackt sie. Fehler immer mit try/catch behandeln.
codeBefore:
fetch("https://example.com")
  .then((r) => r.text())
  .then((t) => console.log(t))
  .catch((e) => console.error(e));
keyPoints: await only inside async functions (or top-level modules).
Unhandled rejections crash logic — use try/catch.
Promise.all for parallel work, like Task.WhenAll.
title: Promises & async/await
tldr: Promise<T> is Task<T>; await unwraps it.

analogy: Like C# namespaces/assemblies: import {x} from './file' ~ using + assembly reference.
analogyDe: Wie C#-Namespaces/Assemblies: import ~ using + Referenz.
audio: Each file is a module. Named exports versus default export. Agents add imports automatically, check the path.
audioDe: Jede Datei ist ein Modul. Benannte Exporte vs. Default. Agents fügen Imports automatisch hinzu, Pfad prüfen.
keyPoints: Prefer named exports; default exports hide names.
Circular imports = smell; same as in C#.
keyPointsDe: Benannte Exporte bevorzugen; Default versteckt Namen.
Zirkuläre Imports = Smell, wie in C#.

quiz.explain: Named import must match the export name.
quiz.explainDe: Benannter Import muss dem Exportnamen entsprechen.
quiz.q: math.ts has `export const add`. Correct import?
quiz.qDe: math.ts hat `export const add`. Korrekter Import?

title: Modules: import/export
tldr: Prefer named exports; paths are relative files.
tldrDe: Benannte Exporte; Pfade sind relative Dateien.

analogy: Like C# static typing but with inference: var x = 5 infers int; same idea, less ceremony.
analogyDe: Wie statische Typisierung in C#, aber mit Inferenz: weniger Zeremonie.
audio: Everyday types: string, number, boolean, arrays, any versus unknown. Let inference do the work.
audioDe: Alltagstypen: string, number, boolean, Arrays, any vs unknown. Inferenz arbeiten lassen.
keyPoints: Annotate where inference is unclear; else let it infer.
unknown = type-safe any: must narrow before use.
keyPointsDe: Annotieren, wo Inferenz unklar; sonst inferieren lassen.
unknown = sicheres any: erst narrowing, dann nutzen.

quiz.explain: any disables checking; unknown forces narrowing.
quiz.explainDe: any schaltet Prüfung ab; unknown erzwingt Narrowing.
options: any skips checks, unknown requires narrowing
optionsDe: any ohne Checks, unknown braucht Narrowing

title: Everyday types
tldr: string/number/boolean + unknown over any.

analogy: interface ~ C# interface; type = alias incl. unions. Structs become object types.
analogyDe: interface ~ C#-Interface; type = Alias inkl. Unions. Structs werden Objekttypen.
audio: Use interface for object shapes agents extend. Use type for unions and helpers. They overlap a lot.
audioDe: interface für Objektformen, type für Unions und Helfer. Viel Überlappung.
keyPoints: interface extends well; type composes unions/intersections.
keyPointsDe: interface gut erweiterbar; type gut kombinierbar.

quiz.q: type Admin = User & { level: number } means…?
quiz.qDe: type Admin = User & { level: number } heißt…?

title: Interfaces vs type
tldr: interface for shapes, type for unions/composition.
tldrDe: interface für Formen, type für Unions/Komposition.

analogy: Like C# pattern matching (is, switch) but via typeof/in/instanceof checks.
analogyDe: Wie Pattern Matching in C# (is, switch), aber mit typeof/in/instanceof.
audio: Narrowing shrinks a union after a check. typeof for primitives, in for shapes, instanceof for classes.
audioDe: Narrowing verkleinert eine Union nach Prüfung. typeof für primitive, in für Formen, instanceof für Klassen.
keyPoints: After a check, TS knows the branch type.
keyPointsDe: Nach Prüfung kennt TS den Zweigtyp.

quiz.explain: typeof string branch → string methods available.

title: Narrowing unions
tldr: Check once, TS knows the type after.
tldrDe: Einmal prüfen, TS kennt danach den Typ.

analogy: Like C# optional params + overloads, but simpler: ? and defaults cover 90%.
analogyDe: Wie optionale Parameter + Überladungen in C#, aber einfacher: ? und Defaults reichen meist.
audio: Optional parameters with question mark. Rest params collect extras. Overloads only for special call shapes.
audioDe: Optionale Parameter mit Fragezeichen. Rest-Parameter sammeln Extras. Overloads nur für Spezialfälle.
codeAfter:
function greet(name = "Ada") { return `hi ${name}`; }
function sum(...nums: number[]) { return nums.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0); }

quiz.explain: Default applies when arg is undefined/missing.

title: Function params that read well
tldr: ? + defaults + rest cover most agent code.
tldrDe: ? + Defaults + Rest decken fast alles ab.

analogy: Like C# generics List<T>: function identity<T>(x: T): T.
analogyDe: Wie Generics in C# List<T>: identity<T>(x: T): T.
audio: Generics keep the input-output link. Constrain with extends. Agents generate them for reusable helpers.
audioDe: Generics erhalten die Ein-Aus-Beziehung. Einschränken mit extends. Agents erzeugen sie für Helfer.
keyPoints: extends constrains: T extends { length: number }.

quiz.explain: T inferred as string, so return is string.
quiz.explainDe: T als string inferiert, Rückgabe string.

title: Generics in 5 minutes
tldr: <T> keeps type flowing; extends constrains.

analogy: | is like C# OneOf / multiple allowed types; & combines like multiple interfaces.
analogyDe: | wie mehrere erlaubte Typen; & kombiniert wie mehrere Interfaces.
audio: Unions list alternatives. Intersections combine. Literals restrict to exact strings.
audioDe: Unions listen Alternativen. Intersections kombinieren. Literale schränken auf exakte Strings ein.
codeBefore:
type ID = string | number;
type Res = { ok: true; v: string } | { ok: false; e: string };
keyPoints: Literal unions restrict strings (great for props).
keyPointsDe: Literal-Unions schränken Strings ein (gut für Props).
title: Unions, intersections, literals
tldr: | = either, & = both, literals = exact values.

analogy: Classes similar to C# but fields need definite assignment (! or init). public/private/protected exist.
analogyDe: Klassen ähnlich C#, aber Felder brauchen Initialisierung (! oder init). public/private/protected existieren.
audio: Class fields must be initialized. Use constructor shorthand with access modifiers. implements checks the shape.
audioDe: Klassenfelder müssen initialisiert sein. Constructor-Shorthand mit Modifizierern. implements prüft Form.

quiz.explain: ! tells TS it will be assigned.
options: Assigned later, suppresses strict init error

title: Classes without surprises
tldr: Init fields or use !; shorthand saves lines.
tldrDe: Felder init oder !; Shorthand spart Zeilen.

analogy: Like C# nullable (string?) — TS has | null and | undefined plus ?.
analogyDe: Wie Nullable in C# (string?) — TS hat | null, | undefined und ?.
audio: Null versus undefined: null is intentional empty, undefined is missing. Optional chaining short-circuits.
audioDe: null ist absichtlich leer, undefined fehlt. Optional Chaining kürzt ab.
codeAfter:
declare const u: { name?: string } | null;
const n = u?.name ?? "guest"; // safe
title: null, undefined, ?. and ??
tldr: ?. + ?? = safe navigation C# knows as ?. and ??.

analogy: Type guards ~ C# 'is' checks returning bool; predicates x is T teach the compiler.
analogyDe: Guards ~ C#-is-Prüfungen; Prädikate x is T belehren Compiler.
audio: Custom guard returns x is Type. assert functions throw on failure. Agents use them for API data.
audioDe: Guard gibt x is Typ zurück. Asserts werfen bei Fehler. Agents nutzen sie für API-Daten.
keyPoints: Return type `x is T` narrows callers.

options: It narrows x to string in true-branch
optionsDe: Verengt x auf string im True-Zweig

title: Type guards (x is T)
tldr: Guards teach TS what your check proved.
tldrDe: Guards sagen TS, was Prüfung bewies.

analogy: Like LINQ Select/Where but compile-time: Partial<T>, Pick<T>, Omit<T>.
analogyDe: Wie LINQ, aber zur Compilezeit: Partial, Pick, Omit.
audio: Utility types transform shapes. Partial makes all optional. Pick selects keys. Readonly freezes.
audioDe: Utility-Typen transformieren Formen. Partial macht alles optional. Pick wählt Keys. Readonly friert ein.
title: Utility types agents love
tldr: Partial/Pick/Omit/Record = shape tools.

analogy: Enums exist in C#; in TS prefer literal unions for props, const objects for maps.
analogyDe: Enums wie in C#; in TS oft Literal-Unions für Props, const-Objekte für Maps.
audio: String enums are readable. Const assertions make literal objects. Agents mix both.
audioDe: String-Enums lesbar. Const-Assertions machen literale Objekte. Agents mischen.
codeAfter:
const Roles = { Admin: "admin", User: "user" } as const;
type Role = typeof Roles[keyof typeof Roles];
codeBefore:
enum Dir { Up = "UP", Down = "DOWN" }
const d: Dir = Dir.Up;

quiz.explain: as const narrows to literal types.
quiz.q: Role type from const object is…?

title: Enums vs literals
tldr: Literals first, enums when behavior attaches.

analogy: await in loops ~ foreach with await in C#; Promise.all ~ Task.WhenAll.
analogyDe: await in Schleifen ~ foreach mit await; Promise.all ~ Task.WhenAll.
audio: Sequential for-of with await is simple. Parallel with Promise dot all is fast. Handle errors per item.
audioDe: Sequentiell mit for-of + await ist einfach. Parallel mit Promise.all schnell. Fehler pro Item behandeln.
codeAfter:
const ids = [1, 2, 3];
const users = await Promise.all(ids.map(fetchUser));
keyPoints: Agents fetch lists in parallel — check error paths.
title: Async patterns in agent code
tldr: for-of = sequential, Promise.all = parallel.

analogy: Like C# LINQ: map=Select, filter=Where, reduce=Aggregate, find=FirstOrDefault.
analogyDe: Wie LINQ: map=Select, filter=Where, reduce=Aggregate, find=FirstOrDefault.
audio: Chain map filter reduce to transform lists. Read agent pipelines left to right.
audioDe: map, filter, reduce verketten. Agent-Pipelines links nach rechts lesen.
codeAfter: const adults = users.filter(u => u.age >= 18).map(u => u.name);
codeBefore:
const total = [1,2,3].reduce((a,b) => a+b, 0); // 6
const found = [1,2,3].find(x => x > 1); // 2
title: map/filter/reduce/find
tldr: LINQ for JS; find can be undefined.
tldrDe: LINQ für JS; find kann undefined sein.

analogy: Structural typing like Go interfaces / C# duck-typing via dynamic — shape matters, not name.
analogyDe: Strukturelle Typisierung wie Go-Interfaces — Form zählt, nicht Name.
audio: TypeScript is structural. Any matching shape is accepted. Excess property checks catch typos in literals.
audioDe: TypeScript ist strukturell. Passende Form wird akzeptiert. Excess-Checks fangen Tippfehler ab.
keyPoints: Missing props error; extra props sometimes ok.
Object literals get strict excess checks.
keyPointsDe: Fehlende Props Fehler; extra teils ok.
title: Structural typing (shape wins)
tldr: Shape matters, not the declared name.

analogy: Reading a diff ~ code review in C#: look at type changes, null paths, and exported API.
analogyDe: Diff lesen ~ Review in C#: Typänderungen, Nullpfade, exportierte API prüfen.
audio: When agents change code, check the type signature first, then null handling, then tests. Ask what changed in the shape.
audioDe: Bei Agent-Änderungen erst Signatur, dann Null-Behandlung, dann Tests prüfen. Fragen: Was änderte sich an der Form?
keyPoints: Widened params = more callers ok; narrowed = break.
Added | null = every caller must branch.
any in diff = red flag; ask for unknown+guard.
keyPointsDe: Weiterer Param = mehr Aufrufer ok; enger = Bruch.
any im Diff = Red Flag; unknown+Guard fordern.
title: Reading agent diffs
tldr: Signature → null → any → exports.

analogy: tsconfig ~ .csproj properties: strict, target, moduleResolution.
analogyDe: tsconfig ~ .csproj-Eigenschaften: strict, target, moduleResolution.
audio: Agents obey tsconfig. Strict true is the goal. Know target lib and module resolution for import errors.
audioDe: Agents gehorchen tsconfig. Strict true ist Ziel. Target und Module-Resolution für Importfehler kennen.
keyPoints: strict: true catches null + implicit any.

quiz.explain: strict enables the family of checks.

title: tsconfig in 3 minutes
tldr: strict true; target + resolution explain errors.
tldrDe: strict true; target + Resolution erklären Fehler.

analogy: any ~ dynamic in C# (no checks); unknown ~ object (must cast/check).
analogyDe: any ~ dynamic (keine Checks); unknown ~ object (muss prüfen/casten).
audio: When agents use any, ask for unknown plus a guard. any spreads like a virus through types.
audioDe: Wenn Agents any nutzen: unknown + Guard fordern. any verbreitet sich wie Virus.
keyPoints: any disables checking for whole chain.
unknown forces a check — safer default.
JSON.parse returns any → wrap to unknown.
keyPointsDe: JSON.parse gibt any → zu unknown wrappen.
title: "any" is the red flag
tldr: See any → ask for unknown + guard.

analogy: ESLint ~ Roslyn analyzers + StyleCop; red squiggles are build breaks in CI.
analogyDe: ESLint ~ Roslyn-Analyzer; rote Wellen = Build-Bruch in CI.
audio: Read errors inside out: property missing, type not assignable, possibly null. Fix the shape, not the symptom.
audioDe: Fehler von innen lesen: Property fehlt, Typ nicht zuweisbar, evtl. null. Form fixen, nicht Symptom.
codeAfter:
// Property 'name' does not exist on type 'User'
// → add name to interface OR fix access
keyPoints: missing prop → typo or stale interface.
title: Top 3 errors agents hit
tldr: possibly null / not assignable / missing prop.
tldrDe: possibly null / not assignable / missing prop.

analogy: npm ~ NuGet; import paths ~ assembly refs; run scripts ~ MSBuild targets.
analogyDe: npm ~ NuGet; Importpfade ~ Assembly-Refs; Scripts ~ MSBuild-Targets.
audio: Agents add packages and imports. Check package json scripts, lockfile changes, and relative import paths.
audioDe: Agents fügen Pakete und Imports hinzu. package.json-Scripts, Lockfile und relative Pfade prüfen.
keyPoints: npm install changes lockfile — review it.
Scripts in package.json = what agents run.
title: npm, scripts & paths
tldr: ./ same dir, ../ up; scripts = agent commands.
